findings.title: `retryCount` delete branch is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.description:
The new `OR` branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` carries no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, so the SMS cron deletes any `WorkflowReminder` with `retryCount > 1`, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP rows. The comment on line 28 still says "delete all scheduled sms reminders".

This is latent today: a repo-wide search shows only this handler writes `retryCount`, so only SMS rows can exceed 1. It becomes silent cross-method data loss as soon as the email or WhatsApp handler adopts the shared column.

Fix by adding `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (and ideally `scheduled: false`) to the second branch, or hoisting `method` above the `OR`.

findings.title: DB update inside `catch` can throw and abort the whole cron run
findings.description:
The `catch` block now awaits `prisma.workflowReminder.update` with no guard of its own. If that update rejects, the error escapes the `for` loop:
- **Remaining reminders are skipped:** every reminder after the failing one in the batch is left unprocessed and the request returns a 500. Before this change the `catch` only logged, so one bad reminder could not stop the batch.
- **Original error is lost:** the `console.log` of the Twilio or rate-limit error sits after the update, so it never runs when the update throws.
- **Likely trigger:** the row can be deleted mid-run, for example by `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` in `smsReminderManager.ts:251` when a booking is cancelled, which makes the update fail with P2025.

Log first, then wrap the retry update in its own try/catch or use `updateMany`.

findings.title: Retry counter uses a stale read-modify-write and conflates failure types
findings.description:
- **Stale increment:** both sites write `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` from the value read at the start of the run. Overlapping cron invocations can lose increments; `data: { retryCount: { increment: 1 } }` is atomic. The same update block is duplicated at lines 179-186 and 190-197.
- **Non-Twilio errors count as retries:** the `try` wraps the whole body, so a failure in `bookingMetadataSchema.parse`, `getBookerBaseUrl`, or the success-path update at line 169 also increments the counter. In the line 169 case Twilio has already accepted the message while `scheduled` stays false, so the next run schedules a duplicate SMS.
- **Non-transient outcomes burn retries:** `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns `undefined` when the user or team is SMS-locked (`twilioProvider.ts:92-95`) and throws on the monthly rate limit (`twilioProvider.ts:97-102`). Either way the reminder is deleted after two cron runs even if the scheduled date is days away. If that is the intent, a comment should say so.
- **One path never counts:** when `message` is empty or `sendTo` is missing (line 158), nothing is incremented, so those reminders are still retried on every run until the scheduled date passes.

findings.title: No tests for the new retry and delete behaviour
New `OR` delete predicate has no supporting index
findings.description: The previous delete could use `@@index([method, scheduled, scheduledDate])` (line 1005). The second `OR` branch filters on `retryCount`, which has no index, so Postgres will most likely fall back to a sequential scan of `WorkflowReminder` on every cron run. Scoping that branch to `method: SMS` and `scheduled: false`, or splitting it into two `deleteMany` calls, lets the existing index be used.

findings.title: Magic retry threshold and inline type widening
findings.description:
- **Threshold:** `gt: 1` encodes "max 2 attempts" as an unnamed literal; a constant such as `MAX_SMS_SCHEDULE_ATTEMPTS` would make the policy explicit.
- **Type:** the cast `as (PartialWorkflowReminder & { retryCount: number })[]` patches the type inline; adding `retryCount` to `PartialWorkflowReminder` and the shared `select` in `getWorkflowReminders.ts` would keep it in one place.
- **Sibling handler:** `scheduleWhatsappReminders.ts` uses the same Twilio scheduling path and still retries without a cap, so the two handlers now diverge.

findings.title: Migration and schema change are safe and consistent
findings.description: `ADD COLUMN "retryCount" INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` matches `retryCount Int @default(0)` at `schema.prisma:1000`. On current Postgres it is a metadata-only change, and existing rows and inserts that omit the field keep working.

New `OR` delete predicate has no supporting index
